faq.q: How is this platform different from AI like Gemini or ChatGPT?
faq.a: This platform is designed specifically for code analysis. You paste or upload code, and the AI instantly gives a score, list of errors, fixes, explanations, and learning tips. Gemini and ChatGPT are general-purpose, while KoreksiKoding focuses on one thing: code.

faq.q: Will my data be used to train AI?
faq.a: No. The code you enter is sent directly to the API provider (Gemini or Groq) for analysis and is not stored or used to train AI models.
KoreksiKoding supports over 20 languages, including Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, C, C++, C#, Go, Rust, PHP, Ruby, Kotlin, Swift, Dart, HTML, CSS, SQL, JSON, XML, and YAML.

faq.q: Is the AI correction always 100% accurate?
faq.a: Not always. The AI helps find common issues and provides fix suggestions, but you should always verify and run the code yourself to confirm the results.

faq.q: How do I report a problem or bug?
faq.a: Please visit our GitHub Issues page and create a new report. Our team will follow up promptly.

faq.q: Is this service free to use?
faq.a: Yes. The platform is free. You only need to set up your own API key from Google AI Studio (Gemini) or Groq Console.

faq.q: Do I need to create an account to start correcting code?
faq.a: No. There is no registration or login. Open the site, enter your API key, and start using it right away.

faq.q: How secure is the code I enter on this platform?
faq.a: Code is never stored on a server. All analysis happens directly through your chosen API provider, and API keys stay stored in your browser.

faq.q: What is the maximum number of lines or characters that can be checked?
faq.a: There is no line limit from the platform. The maximum is determined by the API provider you use. Gemini and Groq typically support up to tens of thousands of tokens per request.

faq.q: Can this platform fix errors automatically (auto-fix)?
faq.a: Yes. After analysis, you can view the corrected code along with a list of changes. You can copy or download the fixed code directly.

logic.title: Programming Logic Basics
logic.desc: Learn flow, conditions, and loops using pseudocode not tied to any language.
items: Sequence: statements execute top to bottom in order
Conditional: make decisions with if/else based on true/false
Loop: repeat actions with for, while, for-each
Functions/procedures: group reusable steps you can call by name
Variables & data types: numbers, text, booleans, store and change values
Operators: arithmetic (+,-,*,/), comparison (==,>,<), logical (AND, OR, NOT)
Pseudocode: describe the algorithm in plain language before coding it

detail.summary: Programming logic is the foundation of algorithmic thinking. It is language-agnostic, build this first, then pick a language.

sections.title: What Is an Algorithm?
sections.content: A logical, ordered set of steps to solve a problem. Each step must be clear and testable.

sections.title: Sequential Flow

sections.title: Branching (Conditions)
sections.content: Use if/else to decide. If the condition is true run branch A, else branch B.

sections.title: Looping
sections.content: Repeat the same action until a condition is met. for for a fixed count, while for a condition.

sections.title: Pseudocode
sections.content: Write steps in plain language first. It keeps focus off syntax and helps design the solution.

debugging.title: Basic Debugging
debugging.desc: Find and fix bugs in your code through a systematic process.
items: Know error types: syntax, runtime, logic
Insert console.log/print to monitor variable values
Isolate: comment out suspected code, then narrow down
Edge cases: test extremes (empty, zero, negative, large)
Reproduce: confirm the error happens consistently

detail.summary: Debugging is not guessing at errors, it is a systematic process of isolation and verification from the message down to reproduction.

sections.title: Print Statements
sections.content: Insert log output to watch variable values during runtime. Remove or replace with a debugger afterward.

sections.title: Isolating the Problem
sections.content: Comment out suspected code blocks. If the error vanishes, that block is guilty. Reduce inputs to a minimum.

sections.title: Testing Edge Cases
sections.content: Bugs often hide at extremes: empty input, zero, negative, or very large data.

security.title: Basic Security
security.desc: Simple practices that prevent common code vulnerabilities.
items: Never hardcode credentials: use .env for API keys, passwords, tokens
Validate input: check type, length, and format before use
SQL injection: use parameterized queries, not string concatenation
XSS: escape HTML output, never render raw user input
HTTPS: encrypt traffic, never send secrets over plain HTTP

detail.summary: Bake in security from the start. Validate all input and never store secrets in code.

sections.title: Input Validation
sections.content: Treat every input as hostile. Validate type, length, and format.

sections.title: SQL Injection
sections.content: Raw string concatenation opens injection attacks. Use parameterized queries.

sections.title: XSS
sections.content: Rendering raw user input runs injected scripts. Escape all HTML output.

sections.title: Secrets Management
sections.content: API keys, passwords, tokens must never be hardcoded. Use env vars or a vault.

sections.title: Transport Security
sections.content: Send sensitive data over HTTPS/TLS, never plain HTTP.
